reconstruction.scope: Specific current Mouse Tower at Bingen: mapped asymmetric main body/projecting eastern stair turret, pale plaster/stone corner pilasters and bands, small genuinely recessed closed windows, projecting corbel gallery/flat deck and open crenellated parapet, taller octagonal shaft/lancet head/closed cap and crenellated crown, sparse iron rods, bounded dark lower housing/hip cap. Four existing shared stucco/raw sandstone/slate/paint graphs. No older red finish, copied heraldry/inscriptions/photo atlas, furnished interior, neighboring castle, whole island mesh or river-covering platform.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Retained map has four building levels and one roof level but no qualified height. Native PMTiles supplies an unqualified14m value, compatible with a level-derived generic body estimate rather than a measurement of the taller head. Picture-led visualization uses main body/corbel13.4..14m, gallery/roof deck17.2m, main crenels18.5m, projecting shaft19.2m, lancet head23.8m/cap24m and crown25m, with sparse iron rods to25.6m. Dimensions/closed-window/reverse/corbel/upper opening inventory and lower housing2.6m cap are explicit estimates, not a conservation survey.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Retain the original6m standard Mapzen ground, native Rhine water polygons/island holes and all independent buildings/paths. Replace only the native tower shell. Bounded buried feet under the original outline meet coarse island grade; no whole-island mesh, broad slab, ground flattening or ground/water cutout. Native terrain/shore resolution and water level are not surveyed bank/flood measurements. Lower housing and roof are within the mapped tower envelope; separate Ehrenfels ruin is native context.
